limits.title: Which places will build
limits.text: Results are statewide totals built from county figures; the tool does not say which towns, neighborhoods or lots will see new homes.

limits.title: How likely each number is
limits.text: Low, middle and high are named assumption sets, not probabilities. Nobody can say that the middle is twice as likely as the low.

limits.title: A turn in the market
limits.text: The baseline range is fitted on history. It held in most past periods, but for forecasts made in 2005-2010, the bust, the actual total fell inside only 56% of the time, and a range drawn at the time would have missed almost every state in 2005-2008.

limits.title: Local rules and local opposition
limits.text: The tool reads state law only. Local zoning, fee schedules, how fast towns issue permits and local opposition are not modeled, and a town can comply with a state law on paper while still slowing building. Every state has an ADU law file; the other four reforms have files for Utah, New Hampshire and Arizona only, so elsewhere their whole benchmark counts as new.

limits.title: Prices, rents and homelessness
limits.text: The tool estimates building permits. It does not estimate prices, rents, affordability, homelessness or who moves in.

limits.title: Permits are not homes
limits.text: A permit is not a finished home; about 79 of every 100 apartment permits and nearly all house permits lead to a finished home. Where the page shows homes, it says how the conversion was made.

limits.title: Homes built without a permit count
limits.text: The Census permit survey misses homes built where no permit is required and many ADU conversions, so the baseline and the ADU increment are not measured the same way.

limits.title: After 2030
limits.text: Every estimate stops at five years; anything a reform produces after 2030 is outside it.

limits.title: Reforms together
limits.text: The combined package is an illustration. No study has measured the five reforms passed together, so the overlaps are removed by stated rules, not by evidence.

limits.title: Bus rapid transit
limits.text: Only rail, streetcar and ferry stops count for transit-oriented density, because the national stop map cannot identify bus rapid transit.

limits.title: Small numbers
limits.text: Increments of a few dozen permits are within the uncertainty of the inputs; read them as "about zero", not as a precise count.

limits.title: The data's date
limits.text: Every figure reflects the data releases listed on the Assumptions and data page (for example, permits through 2025 and the 2020-2024 American Community Survey).
